key_insight: AnyView uses a diffusion-based video generation framework with minimal geometric assumptions to synthesize arbitrary novel viewpoints in highly dynamic real-world scenes, by training on heterogeneous supervision sources.
problem_solved: Bridges the gap between high-quality generative video and strict multi-view + spatiotemporal consistency in dynamic environments, enabling reliable novel-view synthesis without heavy inductive biases or explicit geometric priors.
method: Diffusion-based video generation conditioned for dynamic view synthesis (time + target viewpoint conditioning).
Leverages heterogeneous supervision: monocular 2D, multi-view static 3D, and multi-view dynamic data to learn from varied annotation levels.
Training objectives and architecture choices that encourage multi-view consistency and temporal coherence while keeping minimal geometric assumptions.
impact: Enables more reliable, view-consistent video synthesis for AR/VR, telepresence, robotics, and dataset augmentation, lowering the barrier to synthesize novel views in complex, changing scenes without detailed scene geometry.
visual_elements: High-level architecture diagram: diffusion model block showing conditioning on viewpoint and time.
Before/after panel: input sequence vs synthesized novel viewpoints across time to illustrate spatiotemporal consistency.
Supervision sources infographic: stacked icons for monocular, multi-view static, and multi-view dynamic datasets showing how they feed training.
Quantitative bar/line chart: consistency (multi-view & temporal) and visual quality comparisons vs baselines.
paper_title: AnyView: Synthesizing Any Novel View in Dynamic Scenes
paper_authors: Basile Van Hoorick, Dian Chen, Shun Iwase, Pavel Tokmakov, Muhammad Zubair Irshad
